scope: Proposition 9.4 of the manuscript “A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem” (preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a finite group D act on S = Q i∈I Ti, where all Ti are isomorphic to a nonabelian simple group T, and suppose that its action on I is transitive. Fix i0 ∈ I, set A = Di0 , identify Ti0 with T, and let α : A → Aut(T) be the induced action. The D-invariant subdirect subgroups of S are in bijection with pairs (U, β), where A ≤ U ≤ D, β : U −→ Aut(T), β|A = α. Write S(U, β) for the corresponding subgroup. Then S(U, β) ≤ S(V, γ) ⇐⇒ V ≤ U and β|V = γ. (9.2) In particular, the interval of D-invariant subgroups from S(U, β) to S is anti-isomorphic to [A, U], by restricting β.
